summary.tldr: Raises parole ineligibility for people convicted of abduction, sexual assault and murder of the same victim, and adds jury recommendations and appeal rights.
what_it_does: Creates a new rule for people convicted of abduction, sexual assault and murder of the same victim in the same event or series of events, allowing life imprisonment with no parole eligibility for 25 to 40 years.
Requires the trial judge to ask the jury whether it wants to recommend how many years the person must serve before parole eligibility.
Lets the judge choose a parole ineligibility period above 25 years and up to 40 years, after considering the person’s character, the offences, the circumstances, and any jury recommendation.
Requires the judge to give reasons, orally or in writing, for deciding whether to make the order and for the number of years set.
Allows the convicted person to appeal the order, and allows the Attorney General to appeal a period of less than 40 years or a decision not to make the order.
summary.background: The bill amends the Criminal Code. It adds a new parole rule for cases where one person is convicted of abduction, sexual assault and murder of the same victim.
